parts:
Hello GGIR Community,

Thanks to everyone for their contributions to this excellent resource!

I am setting the analyses for the Axivity data from the UK Biobank.

When piloting the code on two .cwa files, using only parts 1 and 2, I came across the following error:

 _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Part 2

Busy processing ... see /Users/UKBiobank/Results/output_UKBio_Shared/meta/ms2.out for progress

Error in as.character(Value) :

  cannot coerce type 'closure' to vector of type 'character'


I have not come across this error when working with GGIR (reducing ActiGraph data).

If anyone has come across this issue and has a suggestion on how to resolve it, I would appreciate any pointers!

Please find my code below.

Thanks!

Dominika

 

install.packages("devtools", depencies = TRUE)

library(devtools)

remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR")

remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIRread")

 

library(GGIR)

library(GGIRread)

print(load_params())

 

             g.shell.GGIR(

               mode=c(1,2),

               datadir="/Users/UKBiobank/",

               outputdir="/Users/UKBiobank/Results",

               f0=1,

               f1=0,

               idloc=2,

               desiredtz ="Europe/London", # https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones

               interpolationType=1,

               rmc.unit.acc = "g",

               rmc.unit.temp = "C",

               rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",

               rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",

               do.report=c(2),

               rmc.sf=100,

               rmc.doresample=TRUE,

               do.enmo=TRUE,

               do.anglez=TRUE,

               chunksize=1,

               #=====================

               # Part 2

               #=====================

               strategy = 1,

               do.imp=TRUE,

               hrs.del.start = 0,

               hrs.del.end = 0,

               maxdur = 7,

               includedaycrit = 16,

               M5L5res = 10,

               winhr = c(16,8),

               qlevels = c(c(1438/1440),c(1435/1440),c(1430/1440),c(1425/1440),c(1410/1440),c(1380/1440), c(1320/1440)),

               qwindow=c(0,24),

               ilevels = c(0, 50, 100, 400, 8000),

               iglevels = c(seq(0,4000,by=25),8000),

               mvpathreshold = c(100),

               bout.metric = 4,

               boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,

               printsummary=TRUE)

Hi Allison,

I am not able to reproduce your error with GGIR 2.9-4 in Ubuntu. 

The only change I made to your code was to ignore the line:

f1 = as.numeric(length(list.files(shell.input)));f1

because just setting f0 = 1 and f1 = NULL will achieve the same and will adapt to the number of files you provide.

Further, note that the following arguments you specified are not used by GGIR any longer as they have been deprecated: L5M5window and bout.metric.

Did you try running the code in a new output folder or using overwrite = TRUE and deleting the config.csv file generated by GGIR?

If all that does not address the issue, are you sure this example file produces the error?

Thanks,

Vincent

Hi all,

I think I found the problem. It is related to not having either the GGIRread or the read.gt3x package installed, which generates a new object which cause problem with the config file. I have addressed this in a branch of the GGIR github repository, so you can either install that branch:
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue846_bugCharacterGoogleGroup")

Or you can make sure that you have the packages "read.gt3x" and "GGIRread" installed before running your scripts (I know it might be frustrating having to install packages that you don't need, so feel free to install the branch above instead while this fix is incorporated in GGIR).

Please, let us know if this fixes the error.

Best,
Jairo
